result.final_text:
## What this letter says

You had a fall at home and hit your head. You did not lose consciousness.

Your doctor checked you with X-rays and a scan. The X-ray showed no fracture of your right hip. The scan showed no bleeding inside your head.

Your blood pressure was measured lying down and standing up. Your blood pressure drops too much when you stand up. This is called postural hypotension (blood pressure drops when standing up). Your amlodipine medicine may be making this happen.

## What you need to do

1. Stop taking amlodipine. It may be making your blood pressure drop when you stand.
2. Continue all your other medicines.
3. When you stand up, do it slowly.
4. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand up.

## Dates and medicines

Amlodipine 10 mg - STOP

Your GP will check your blood pressure again in 4 weeks.

The Falls Prevention Clinic will write to you with an appointment.

## Questions to ask your doctor

1. Why do I need to stop amlodipine?
2. How can I prevent falling again?
3. When will my blood pressure be checked again?

## When to get urgent help

If you develop a worsening headache, vomiting, confusion or drowsiness in the next few days, call 999 or go to A&E.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
